- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) or shows strong reversal, model often overshoots downward; adjust upward to avoid premature sell-off.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects downward; delay or reduce downward adjustment.
- If model shows strong upward trend but sentiment is mixed or negative, cap forecast growth to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Mean reversion is more pronounced in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — model often overreacts; dampen early forecast slopes.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in direction — align forecast with sentiment momentum rather than historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period price peaks; reduce forecast tail end if sentiment is cooling or neutral.
